blocks.text: We are very glad to welcome Nancy Burgess, who joins Quillon Harbor Advisors as an Analyst in Advisory and will spend most of her time on our fairness opinion work and the board-facing material that travels with it, where her habit of citing every input and footnoting every assumption is exactly what the work asks of us. Nancy reports to Mark Allen, Partner, who will set her assignments, read her drafts first, and be the person she brings any question about a source or a number to, however small it seems.

rows: Comparable-company and precedent-transaction analyses in support of fairness opinions, with every input cited to its source
Mark Allen and the deal team assigned to each opinion
Nancy builds the first version; Mark Allen reviews the sources and the choice of comparables before any of it is shown to a board
Drafts of board-facing material: the summary of the process, the analyses behind it, and the supporting exhibits
Mark Allen, with a final read by Heather Delacruz before any opinion or board book leaves the firm
Drafts go to Mark Allen first and come back marked up; the redline stays in the file alongside the version that went out
The assumptions log for each analysis, including a note wherever a figure has been rounded and on what basis
The analysts and associates working the same mandate
Kept current as the model changes, so that anyone who picks up the file can see why each number is what it is
Screening support on buy-side search programs when a program needs another analyst
The analyst group in Advisory, as Mark Allen assigns it
Taken on only when Mark Allen moves her onto it, so the opinion work keeps its place in her week
Describing targets by sector and revenue band in anything that circulates outside the deal team
Everyone at the firm

blocks.text: Nancy's first review will be with Mark Allen once she has carried her first assignment, whether an opinion or a set of board materials, from the first data request through to the board, since this work arrives on a board's timetable and a finished piece tells us more than a date on the calendar would. Mark Allen will go through her drafts alongside the comments they drew, ask her to walk him through one analysis from its sources to its conclusion, and ask what she would change about how the work was set up, which makes it as much a review of how we staffed the assignment as of how she handled it. Before any of that, the one step we ask of her is to bring Mark Allen the assumptions log from her first assignment by the end of her first week, so the two of them can agree early on how much footnoting is enough.

Quillon Harbor Advisors is a mergers and acquisitions advisory firm working in the lower middle market, and most of what we do comes down to helping an owner, a sponsor, or a board make one consequential decision with a clear view of the alternatives in front of them. We run sell-side processes for founder-owned industrial and business-services companies, conduct buy-side search programs for private-equity platforms building a position in a sector, and, when a board needs an independent read on a proposed transaction, prepare a fairness opinion. Our deal teams are small on purpose, so the people an owner meets in the first conversation are the people who write the materials, take the buyers' calls, and stay with the process through to signing.
Our work, by capability and sector

rows: Sell-side advisory

Preparing the company and its financial information for market, drafting the confidential information memorandum, building a list of strategic and financial buyers, and managing the process from first outreach through indications of interest, letters of intent, diligence, and signing.
Founder-owned industrial companies, including manufacturers, fabricators, and distributors, and business-services companies, most often where the founder is selling the business for the first time.
Buy-side search programs

Defining a universe of candidate targets with the sponsor, screening it against the platform's criteria, approaching the companies that pass, executing NDAs with those willing to talk, and carrying the strongest candidates to an offer, with the state of the funnel set out plainly at every stage.
Private-equity platforms consolidating a fragmented sector, most often in the same industrial and business-services markets where we run sell-side work.
Fairness opinions

An independent opinion to the board on whether the consideration in a proposed transaction is fair, from a financial point of view, supported by the valuation analyses and a complete record of the inputs and assumptions behind them.
Boards of directors and special committees, typically of privately held companies, on transactions where our independence is not in question.

blocks.text: Whichever side of a transaction we are on, we report progress in numbers, because a process is a funnel and the client should be able to watch it narrow. A seller hears each week how many parties have been contacted, how many have signed a non-disclosure agreement, and how many remain in the process, and a sponsor running a search with us sees the same arithmetic from the other direction, from the size of the universe through the screen to the companies that have agreed to talk. We do not describe a stage as reached until it has been, and when a number moves the wrong way we say so in the same report that would have carried the better news.

The clients we have worked for include {{fact:f:E-2014-001.client}}, {{fact:f:E-2015-001.client}}, {{fact:f:E-2016-001.client}}, and {{fact:f:E-2018-001.client}}, along with {{fact:f:E-2019-001.client}}, {{fact:f:E-2021-001.client}}, {{fact:f:E-2022-001.client}}, and {{fact:f:E-2023-001.client}}. We name them as a sample of the range of our work and not as a full account of it, and most of our relationships begin the same way, with a question from an owner, a sponsor, or a board about what a process would involve and what it would ask of them. Where a client has asked that its name stay out of material of this kind, it does, and its absence here should not be read as a gap in the work.

We treat confidentiality as a working habit and not only as a clause in an agreement. In anything that circulates beyond a deal team, a target is described by its sector and revenue band and is named only where the document is already privileged, and every engagement letter and fairness opinion is read by Heather Delacruz, our Managing Partner, before it leaves the firm, with particular attention to any sentence that promises more than the process can deliver.

An owner, sponsor, or board weighing a transaction can begin with a conversation with Heather Delacruz, who will set out how a process would run, what it would ask of the company and its management, and what we would need to see before recommending that one begin. If both sides then want to go further, the next step is a short written proposal from us setting out the scope of the work, the team that would do it, and the terms of an engagement letter.
